title: Finding Harry Carney a mouthpiece
summary: Royal took Carney to a repairman and he chose the mouthpiece he used throughout his career.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You were telling me a story about how Harry Garney (PHONETIC) got the right mouthpiece.

Yes, Harry came out here -- I don't remember whether it was the first or the second time he came into California, and he seemed to be having trouble with the mouthpiece that he had because it wasn't open enough. He wasn't able to put everything into it that he wanted to put into it. So at the time, I was playing baritone saxophone, as well as

alto saxophone, because that was the double of that particular era, both of the horns are in the same pitch, the same key, I should say, E-flat. So most of the fellows that played alto saxophone also played baritone because they could play off the same music and get various harmonies. So Harry asked me to try to find him a mouthpiece. So I took him to my man, who was at that time noted as being positively the best repairman in town, a fellow by the name of George Teak (PHONETIC). He was downtown on Spring Street and I took him down and he handed Harry a whole handful of mouthpieces. So we sat down there for about two hours, exchanging ideas about the mouthpieces and such, until Harry finally indoctrinated himself on this particular mouthpiece. That particular mouthpiece that he bought, he ended using it for his entire career.
You say it cost about six dollars.
Yeah, somewhere around six, seven dollars.
And you led him to it when he was here in Los Angeles?
Yep, my good deed for the day.
